title: Monodromy for norm-topology continuous coefficients on normal schemes
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-algebraic-closure] with the topology of the extended $\ell$-adic absolute value. Let $X$ be a nonempty connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] separated Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with $\ell$ invertible in every local ring. Noetherian means locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact. Assume that each local ring of $X$ is an integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $\Pi=\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,\bar x)$ be the profinite etale fundamental group [def-galois-fibre-functor]. For $K=\Omega$ or any finite intermediate extension $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq K\subseteq\Omega$, give $K$ its restricted norm topology and put $R_{K,X}=p_X^*C(-,K)$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and lisse in the finite locally free sense [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module].

There are $K$-linear equivalences $\Phi_K$ between lisse $R_{K,X}$-modules and continuous finite-dimensional $K$-linear representations of $\Pi$. Here a representation is a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $V$ with product norm topology in a basis and a homomorphism $\rho:\Pi\to\operatorname{GL}_K(V)$ whose matrix entries are continuous; arrows are equivariant $K$-linear maps. The equivalences send the regular module to the trivial representation $K$, finite direct sums to finite direct sums, and include dimension zero. They are compatible with each inclusion $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ for finite $E$: there is an isomorphism, natural in every lisse $R_{E,X}$-module $L$,
$$\Phi_\Omega\bigl(R_{\Omega,X}\otimes_{R_{E,X}}L\bigr)\cong\Omega\otimes_E\Phi_E(L),$$
where tensor on the left is ordinary internal scalar extension [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] along the ring map obtained by postcomposition with $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ and pullback [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. The right side has action $g(a\otimes v)=a\otimes\rho(g)v$. In particular the scalar-extended module on the left is lisse. All continuous $\Omega$-valued functions are used; no finite-subextension-valued restriction is imposed.

proof.text: Apply normal_generic_lisse_cocycle to obtain integrality and the normalized, additive, fully faithful generic-section functor for every ultrametric coefficient field. The given norm equality on Q_l bounds every natural-number norm by one in Omega, so the norm is ultrametric; the induced norm on each intermediate field is ultrametric as well.

proof.text: Choose the canonical separable closure inside the algebraic closure of the function field, and a small profinite model of the finite-etale fundamental group at the resulting generic point. The normal Galois presentation supplies the canonical continuous surjection q. Identify its small fundamental group with the automorphisms of the FLC fibre functor and conjugate by one geometric path to the prescribed basepoint. The resulting group isomorphism c is chosen once for all coefficient fields.

proof.text: For each generic-section representation, choose a finite basis and apply the completed-frame comparison. Its kernel clause shows the action kills ker(q). Descend the action through the surjective group homomorphism c q, leaving its vector space unchanged. Continuity of every matrix coordinate descends because a continuous surjection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a quotient map. Keep the original linear maps on arrows: intertwining descends and reflects along a surjection, giving a fully faithful additive functor.

source.place: Assembly of Bhatt--Scholze 7.4.7 and 7.4.10 with the norm-topology generic, completion, associated-module and scalar-comparison lemmas.

proof.text: For a continuous finite-dimensional representation choose a finite basis, write its continuous homomorphism into GL_n, and restrict it through c. The compact-torsor associated-module lemma supplies a lisse module and a generic section basis with exactly these matrices after q. Transport this basis through the normalized generic-section identification. Equality of all matrix entries gives an equivariant linear isomorphism to the original representation, so the functor is essentially surjective. Its equivalence inverse is additive. The normalized generic scalar-map clause, faithfulness and the equivalence counit formula give precisely linearity of the inverse on underlying sheaf arrows. The generic regular-module isomorphism descends through the same quotient. Empty bases are permitted in every construction.

proof.text: For each finite intermediate field, take its actual continuous inclusion into Omega. Use the existing ordinary lisse extension functor. Tensor the source section identification with Omega, compose with the natural generic scalar comparison, and compose with the inverse target section identification. Apply target section injectivity to check naturality. Lift each fundamental-group element through c q and apply the generic Galois-equivariance equation to check equivariance on pure tensors. These give NormContinuousScalarComparison for the one Omega equivalence and every finite intermediate field.
